title: [observability] a delivered task says what its worker did since it reached it: /api/missions' activity (its worker's latest engine event since the delivery and the tool calls it started since), shown under the stepper and in the task panel (GitHub #63 part 1)
prompt:
Spawn, objective 211 [observability] (GitHub #63 part 1, filed 2026-11-16 on mission 2: "a delivered task looks stalled for 30-70 minutes"; lead's scope approval of 2026-11-17 14:4x; author rev-j): a delivered task says what its worker did since the task reached it.

Base: live main a599100c.

The problem: a task's stages are assigned, delivered, reported, reviewed. Execution dominates (1914-3202 s on mission 2) and between delivered and reported the board had no signal at all: tasks 12, 13 and 17 sat in delivered for 30-74 minutes with nothing to tell working from hung. The data is in the worker's session; /api/missions did not surface it.

Read first:
- crates/spawn-postgres/src/missions.rs (MISSION_BOARD, LAST_GATES: a read kept out of the board because the supervisor's login reads the board and may not read spawn_events; STALL_FACTS' sessions);
- crates/spawn-core/src/observe/snapshot.rs (note_times: the Observer's progress is the engine's own events, source claude);
- crates/spawn-core/src/bridge.rs (the Bridge records a busy pane's screen.observed again every refresh);
- crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (missions(), with_last_gates);
- web/src/components/missions/MissionsView.tsx (TaskRow, StageSteps), web/src/components/missions/TaskPanel.tsx.

What changes:
(1) A new read, PostgresStore::task_activity (crates/spawn-postgres/src/activity.rs, TASK_ACTIVITY): every task in state delivered with a session, keyed by task id, {since_ms, at_ms, event, tool_calls}: since_ms the time of its latest task.delivered record (a task sent back and delivered again counts from the latest delivery); at_ms and event its session's latest engine output (source claude, as its transcript gives it: model.usage, tool.started, tool.completed, tool.failed, turn.stopped, turn.failed, job.started, job.ended) after that record, both null when there is none; tool_calls its session's tool.started events (source claude) after that record. After is by event id. Never the Bridge's screen.observed (a pane stuck on a spinner is refreshed as busy), the Observer's judgements or a checkpoint; never the engine's input either: message.received (a user line: a prompt reaching the engine) and message.taken (the engine taking a typed command's marker) come at +0 s after every delivery as the brief arrives, so a worker hung right after its brief would read as having moved.
(2) GET /api/missions: each task carries activity, that object for a delivered task, null for every other task. Read through the reader login, as LAST_GATES is, and kept out of MISSION_BOARD.
(3) The Missions page: a delivered task's card row shows a line under its stepper, and the timeline's task panel the same line: "last output 4m ago (tool.completed) · 12 tool calls since delivery", or "no output in the 31m since delivery"; in the warning tone once no engine event came for 10 minutes or more (web/src/taskActivity.ts).

Cost: one more read per /api/missions answer, polled. It is bounded by the delivered tasks and their tool calls since delivery, never by how long a session is: per delivered task, the delivery record by spawn_events_control_record, the latest engine event as one backward step of the (session_id, event_name, id) index per engine event name down to the record's id, and the tool calls as that index's range over the session's tool.started from the record's id. No store change, no new index.

What stays as it is:
- every other field of /api/missions, the stages, the stepper's steps and durations;
- the dispatcher's stall rules and their latest fact (STALL_FACTS);
- MISSION_BOARD, which the supervisor's login reads.

Files: crates/spawn-postgres/src/activity.rs (new), crates/spawn-postgres/src/lib.rs (its mod line), crates/spawn-postgres/tests/activity.rs (new), crates/spawn-cli/src/serve.rs (missions, with_activity, a unit test), web/src/taskActivity.ts (new), web/src/missions.ts, web/src/components/missions/TaskActivity.tsx (new), web/src/components/missions/MissionsView.tsx (TaskRow), web/src/components/missions/TaskPanel.tsx, web/test/taskActivity.test.ts (new); owner: rsi/scenarios/211.sh, rsi/backlog/211.json.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/211.sh, black box through GET /api/missions on a fresh spawn serve, the history and the workers' events seeded as the store records them.
- (1) Task 1, delivered 60 min ago to worker a, whose engine started a call before the delivery, then took the brief (message.received, message.taken) and started two calls and ended one after it, followed by a busy pane the Bridge read and an Observer judgement: activity {since_ms: its task.delivered record's time, at_ms: the ended call's time, event: tool.completed, tool_calls: 2}.
- (2) Task 2, delivered 30 min ago to worker b, whose engine then took the brief (message.received and message.taken, as live at +0 s after every delivery) and nothing more, after which only the Bridge read its pane: {since_ms: its delivery, at_ms: null, event: null, tool_calls: 0}.
- (3) Task 3 (reported) and task 4 (assigned): activity null.
- (4) Worker b's engine then ends a turn: task 2's activity is that turn end (turn.stopped, tool_calls 0); task 1's is unchanged.
On live main a599100c 211.sh exits 1 at (1): /api/missions has no activity. A task sent back and delivered again, each engine output name (and the same name from the Bridge, which is none), the brief arriving after a delivery (none) and a Bridge tool.started (no call), and the reader login's read are covered by crates/spawn-postgres/tests/activity.rs.

Not in 211 (#63's other parts, later contracts): refusing or merging a duplicate brief in flight (212), and the paper cuts (213).

Verified by: the gate runs 211.sh. Live, a delivered task's card on the Missions page shows when its worker last moved and its tool calls since delivery.
